docs.title: Mentoring a Junior Colleague
docs.text: Field Content Date 17 Aug 2026 Activity Mentoring Duration 30 mins Objective Provide constructive career advice Session Focus After learning I would be leaving my R2 role, an R1 colleague reached out for advice. They had been asked if they were interested in being my replacement but gave a non-committal answer. They were waiting on the outcome of another slightly more advanced R1 role and also had interview fatigue after recently losing out for another open R2 position. I advised them to call our manager back, express strong interest in the R2 role, and explain that their hesitation was due to not wanting to turn down the better R1 role if offered. I explained that honesty is the best policy. It is fine to say the R2 role is their priority, while accepting the R1 role in the meantime so they do not risk ending up with neither. Reflection I felt I may have been too forceful and next time will be less concrete "do this" and more "this is an option". However, the colleague ended the call by thanking me for revitalising their enthusiasm and said they would take my advice. Evidence None, informal ad-hoc teams call

docs.title: Create Whitebox Pentesting Process Content
docs.text: Field Content Date 18 Aug 2026 Activity Content creation Duration 2 hours Objective Create a clear whitebox pentesting process summary and share an accessible version publicly Session Focus Completed a second pass of the whitebox pentesting process and published the first page covering the four main stages: code review, local testing, proof of concept, and patching/remediation. Also used AI to turn the content into an infographic and posted it on LinkedIn. Reflection Writing the process out forced me to structure and clarify my own methodology. Creating the LinkedIn version helped me practise explaining technical processes in a more accessible way. Both the detailed page and the public post will support future knowledge sharing and reinforce the material for myself. Evidence https://variable190.github.io/dans-cyber-stuff/whitebox-testing/process/ and https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7495670416015872000/

docs.title: Create Node/Express Code Review Overview Content
docs.text: Field Content Date 19 Aug 2026 Activity Content creation Duration 4 hours Objective Create a practical Node/Express code review guide and deepen my understanding of how Express handles requests Session Focus Wrote a step-by-step whitebox code review page for Node/Express covering entry points, global middleware, route mounting, endpoint tracing, and dependency checks. Worked through how express.json() parses request bodies, how cors() sets response headers, the difference between path prefixes and endpoints, how require and destructuring imports work, and the full request flow from server to controller. Reflection Building the page forced me to properly understand the request lifecycle instead of just recognising patterns. I can now clearly explain where client input enters (req.body, query, params, headers), how routes are registered versus how they are executed, and where dangerous sinks are likely to appear. This will improve both my code review quality and my ability to explain findings. Evidence https://variable190.github.io/dans-cyber-stuff/whitebox-testing/node-express-code-review/

docs.title: Create CPD Log
docs.text: Field Content Date 19 Aug 2026 Activity Creating a CPD log Duration 2 hours Objective Design a structured, public CPD record aligned with UK CSC requirements Session Focus Set up a new MkDocs GitHub Pages site. Defined top-level categories (Structured Learning, Reflective Learning, Professional Contribution). Designed a consistent entry template covering date, activity, duration, objective, session focus, reflection and evidence. Refined the format through several iterations to keep it clear, concise and suitable for professional registration evidence. Reflection Building this forced me to think carefully about how CPD evidence should be presented. The process of choosing categories and writing the first entries improved my understanding of what assessors look for. I now have a repeatable system that will make future CPD recording quicker and more consistent. Evidence https://variable190.github.io/cpd/

docs.title: HTB Academy Senior Web Penetration Tester path
docs.text: Field Content Date 18 Aug 2026 Activity Formal course Duration 6 months Objective Complete the Senior Web Penetration Tester Job Role Path and build advanced web application penetration testing skills Session Focus Covered advanced web application penetration testing techniques with a strong focus on whitebox testing and code analysis. Key areas included injection attacks (SQL, NoSQL, XPath, LDAP), authentication and session management flaws (JWT, OAuth, SAML), XSS and CSRF exploitation, HTTP request smuggling, SSRF, DNS rebinding, WebSocket attacks, deserialization vulnerabilities, prototype pollution, and secure code review. Reflection After this first pass ver the content I feel I have understood the material but do not yet have a deep understanding. I will reinforce my learning by creating tutorial content and doing deep dives on specific exploits related to the various vulnerabilities. This knowledge will be directly useful in my new bug bounty triage role starting next month and I also expect to pass elements of it on to associate analysts. Evidence https://academy.hackthebox.com/achievement/1420202/path/405
